correctness.rationale: Recomputed derivative in radial/tangential frames as u times orthogonal rotation times shear [[1,0],[k(r),1]], k(r)=2eta r²/(1+r²)². Singular norm is u(sqrt(1+k²/4)+|k|/2); |k| attains |eta|/2 precisely at r=1, which proves both global exact Lipschitz boundary and its necessity from a maximizing local singular vector. At equality ||DF||=1 only on the unit circle, so every nondegenerate straight segment has strict derivative norm bound a.e. and gives |F(z)-F(w)|<|z-w|. Because u*<1 for eta!=0, bounded forward orbits and invariant large disks provide a fixed point by Brouwer; strict distance decrease gives uniqueness and compactness forces global convergence. Independently checked reciprocal radical identity for eta=.5,2,6,13, with u*(6)=(sqrt(13)-3)/2. No finite test stands for global chord/compactness proof.
residual_risks: The theorem certifies sharp nonexpansiveness, not the sharp global asymptotic stability region above u*.
eta=0 is excluded, necessarily for endpoint uniqueness.

value.rationale: This is an exact sharp, forcing-independent robustness frontier for a naturally parameterized optical nonlinear map; the endpoint provides a nontrivial global-convergence theorem even without a uniform contraction constant. The result answers a structural dynamical question, not merely a routine differential-norm numerical estimate.
residual_risks: No claim of instability above the nonexpansiveness frontier or optimal convergence rate.

final_claim: For eta nonzero and u>=0, the saturating Ikeda plane map is globally Euclidean nonexpansive iff u<=sqrt(1+eta^2/16)-|eta|/4, and globally strictly Lipschitz-contracting iff u is less; at equality pairwise strict contraction and global convergence to the unique fixed point still hold.
limitations: eta nonzero; u nonnegative; full Euclidean plane, not a general global-attraction threshold.
Older Ikeda and control papers lack complete full-text comparisons.
